record.brief:
Create index.html, a complete single-file offline expense log for a small business.
Use no accounts, external libraries, fonts, or network requests. Make it readable on a phone.
The form has accessible labels Description, Amount, and Category. Category choices are
Supplies, Travel, Meals, and Other. Its button says Add expense. Show an expense table
with Description, Amount, Category, and a Delete button on each expense row.
Show Total: $0.00 initially; display dollars with two decimal places and keep the total
correct after adding and deleting entries. Reject a blank description, zero or negative
amount, and nonnumeric amounts, showing an accessible inline error with role=alert.
Descriptions are plain text even when they contain HTML characters. Save entries on
this computer with localStorage. Reloading must preserve added entries and deletions.
Build actual working files using small SQLite steps for form validation, the expense
table/totals, and persistence. Save and run a repeatable verifier that exercises real
form input and checks persistence across page reload. Keep PLAN.md and PROGRESS.md accurate.

interpretation: Interrupted and resumed evolving-code development trials; not a controlled comparison or unassisted fresh build.
Initial run did produce an app and valid five-step plan before deliberate interruption; earlier no-app snapshot was stale.
A resumed run deferred automatically for live user music; its exact-label grader timeout was a harness limitation, not evidence of broken app labels.
A verified native-validation diagnostic was supplied through task memory; app source was not manually repaired.

Latest resumed run made 24 calls but did not complete any of its five SQL units. Eight observed browser checks passed; reload persistence failed. Later checks were not reached after deletion target timeout.
General app-building reliability remains unproven. Token/call/time totals are per completed report, not the full interrupted development session.
No model approval, ranking, or cloud eligibility was changed.
next_investigations: Repair actual persistence and deletion behavior without weakening user requirements.
Make native split-step shorthand resolve safely against the exact seen active unit; latest trial omitted step_id.

DescriptionAmountCategoryAction

interpretation: Assisted evolving-code resume, not an unassisted fresh build or controlled speed comparison.
Developer supplied an actual row-delete browser test and retained its failing cases without editing app source. Both diagnostic receipts are included in the raw report.
After two local calls the benchmark deferred for a real music worker. Raw run_outcome failed is historical runner labeling; inference_error establishes the defer, not a completed app attempt.
All 15 independent browser checks ran; 12 passed. Deletion, saved deletion, and later decimal totals still failed. Three SQL units remain complete and two unfinished.
The baseline verifier failed. Mutation tests were deliberately not run because rejection by an already failing verifier cannot prove correctness.
Subsequent benchmark code labels media deferrals explicitly and checks live media before internal inference retries. An already in-flight request is not cancelled.
No full-app completion claim or model ranking change.

The later resume made six recorded local calls in 369.48 worker seconds before another live music worker triggered an explicit deferred outcome. Three SQL units remain complete; 14 of 15 browser checks passed but the baseline verifier still failed.

Deletion works immediately after reload, then fails after render replaces the buttons. An additional unchanged-source lifecycle check proves the first deletion succeeds and the second fails. The decimal-total check includes such a later deletion; do not infer an arithmetic-only defect.
The retained suite is at its bounded sequence capacity. Scalable test retention/consolidation needs investigation; do not silently drop earlier failing cases or assertions to declare success.

validation.history: The combined run passed all 109 browser tests but exposed one native compaction regression. It was fixed without changing that test; the full 180 native tests then passed.

interpretation: Resumed evolving-code assisted development trials. No app source was manually repaired, but developer browser diagnostics and acceptance cases were supplied and retained.

The first run exhausted schema correction without a valid router completion. Its API requests still consumed local tokens; model_calls counts valid router responses, while upstream_local_calls records actual inference requests.

The second run recorded 11 valid responses, 12 router attempts and 14 upstream calls in 264.71 worker seconds. The new shape-only receipts show malformed quoted step lists with trailing extra data and valid actual arrays. No automatic malformed-JSON repair was added.

The second run split the plan into six units, with three complete, and regressed deletion. Twelve of 15 independent browser checks pass; saved verifier fails. This does not demonstrate reliable app construction or a controlled speed gain.

Retained cases beyond the old eight-sequence / 24-case ceiling are preserved. Shared-browser tests prove sequence isolation; local report receipts preserve complete metadata when stdout would exceed its budget.

Structured step results now retain failed inputs and expectations without an escaped raw verifier transcript. The old transcript remains in historical evidence; no claim that this alone fixes model reasoning.

Next investigations should change the failing repair approach: focused readable-source diagnosis / source-edit workflow and measured model suitability, rather than repeating the same broad prompts or weakening saved checks.

validation.history: An earlier run passed 305 tests and failed the old eight-sequence limit assertion. That test now checks the actual expanded boundary; new overflow/preservation tests cover both capacity limits. The final full run passed all 307.
